chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, son of Yahya, from Muhammad, son of Ahmad, from one of his companions, from Al-Hasan, son of Ali, son of Abu Uthman, from Muhammad, son of Uthman, from Muhammad, son of Hammad Al-Khazzaz, from Abdul Aziz Al-Qarataysi, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abdul Aziz! Faith (Iman) consists of ten levels, like a ladder, from which one ascends step by step. So let not the one on the second step say to the one on the first, “You are not upon anything,” until he reaches the tenth. So do not dismiss the one who is below you, lest the one who is above you dismiss you. And when you see someone who is lower than you by a level, raise him to you with gentleness, and do not burden him with what he cannot endure, lest you break him. For whoever breaks a believer, upon him is its repair (or consequence).'
ai.seo_question: What are the ten levels of faith and how should believers interact with each other according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the hierarchical nature of faith (Iman) as a ten-tiered ladder, warning against spiritual arrogance where those at lower levels dismiss those below them. He prescribes a gentle, supportive approach to uplifting others, emphasizing that causing a believer to falter creates a spiritual debt of repair, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical teachings on communal cohesion and the preservation of the soul's spiritual state.
